Convert, map, sum, intersect, and project sets

Ready · installed consumers

Follow each installed operation from its complete input representation to its output. Conversion changes representation, a Minkowski sum combines sets, H intersection adds constraints, and a nominal predecessor asks which states can reach the target under an admissible control.

Mathematical input

Scalar H intersection input
inequality rowbound
x ≤ 11
−x ≤ 00

Result. The four installed clients return: H-to-V and V-to-H conversion of [0,1]²; the Minkowski sum [0,1]+[0,1]=[0,2]; the H intersection [0,1]; and the nominal predecessor {x : ∃u∈[−1,1], x+u=2}=[1,3].

Reproduce this result

Full input description and JSON

Convert the unit square between H and V forms. Compute [0,1]+[0,1]. Intersect x≤1 with −x≤0. Compute the nominal predecessor {x : ∃u∈[−1,1], x+u=2}.

Open the structured chapter manifest JSON

Command

ctest --test-dir build/dev -C Release -R "^installed_public_client$" --output-on-failure
build/dev/installed-consumer/build/installed_conversion_client
build/dev/installed-consumer/build/installed_affine_sum_client
build/dev/installed-consumer/build/installed_polyhedral_intersection_client
build/dev/installed-consumer/build/installed_projection_predecessor_client

Expected output

Installed Qhull conversion client: H-to-V square vertices passed
Installed Qhull conversion client: V-to-H square inequalities passed
Installed affine/sum client: selected LP and hull providers produced a numerical set result
Installed polyhedral client: public H intersection passed
Installed predecessor client: existential integrator interval and unestablished support passed

Intermediate geometry. H-to-V returns the four unit-square corners. V-to-H returns the four unit-square bounds. The interval sum is [0,2]. The H intersection is [0,1] with two rows. The existential predecessor is [1,3]; the consumer accepts 1 and 3 but rejects 0.875 and 3.125.

Support limits. Qhull conversion and affine sums use numerical providers and bounded client inputs. The predecessor has unestablished support assurance. The projection demonstrates an existential predecessor for one scalar integrator, not a general full-state intersection. Projected overlap does not prove full-state intersection. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).
